description: Future offshore wind projects in deeper areas of the Atlantic Outer Continental Shelf may use floating wind technology
geographic_scope: Deeper areas of the Atlantic Outer Continental Shelf
context_quote: BOEM anticipates completing the review of 16 OSW projects by 2025. All these projects are anticipated to have fixed foundation turbines, though future leasing plans in deeper areas of the Atlantic OCS contemplate the use of floating technology, which could help contribute to the goal of 15 GW of floating OSW by 2035.

description: Offshore wind projects must avoid or minimize known and potential impacts to North Atlantic right whales (NARWs) and their habitat
geographic_scope: Areas proposed for offshore wind development
context_quote: Given the uncertainty in the potential effects of the presence and operation of OSW facilities on protected species and their habitats (Dorrell et al. 2022; Raghukumar et al. 2023), management of OSW development should proceed with a focus on avoiding or minimizing known and potential impacts to NARWs and their habitat.

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whale critical habitat
geographic_scope: North Atlantic right whale critical habitat
context_quote: NARWs inhabit the waters of the U.S. and Canadian Atlantic, with some parts of their range designated as critical habitat under the ESA (81 FR 4838, January 27, 2016) and Canada's Species At Risk Act (Fisheries and Oceans Canada 2014).

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whale high-use areas for important life history functions such as foraging, migrating, mating, or calving
geographic_scope: North Atlantic right whale high-use areas
context_quote: Within the areas proposed for OSW development in the United States, NARWs engage in migration, foraging, socializing, reproduction, calving, and resting behaviors critical to their survival (Leiter et al. 2017; Muirhead et al. 2018; Quintana-Rizzo et al. 2021; Zoidis et al. 2021).

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whales during their seasonal presence in different regions
geographic_scope: Regions with seasonal North Atlantic right whale presence
context_quote: In the Atlantic OCS off the southeast United States, NARW presence is highly seasonal as evident in monthly density maps (Appendix D), with NARWs mostly present between November and May. In the Atlantic OCS off the northeast and Mid-Atlantic regions, NARWs are present year-round (Davis et al. 2017).

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whales from noise, vessel strikes, entanglement, and changes to habitat and prey availability
context_quote: The four primary stressors identified in this Strategy include the following (in no particular order): 1) Exposure to noise, 2) Strikes from vessels, 3) Entanglement, and 4) Changes to habitat.

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whales from cumulative effects of multiple projects
geographic_scope: Areas with multiple offshore wind projects
context_quote: Effects to NARWs could result from stressors generated from a single project; there is potential for these effects to be compounded by exposure to multiple projects. NARWs migrating along the U.S. Atlantic Coast have the potential to travel near or through many currently proposed OSW developments along the Atlantic Coast.

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whales in designated critical habitat areas
geographic_scope: North Atlantic right whale critical habitat
context_quote: For example, if the OSW development being considered in the Gulf of Maine moves forward, it would occur in designated NARW critical habitat (Leiter et al. 2017; O'Brien et al. 2022; Quintana-Rizzo et al. 2021; Stone et al. 2017).

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whales that could lead to population-level consequences, including both lethal and sublethal effects
context_quote: Sublethal effects can be direct or indirect, and often scientific quantification of indirect effects is challenging, though some can be modeled. Whales that are in compromised condition (e.g., injured, entangled, malnourished) and exposed to stressors are likely to experience more severe consequences than healthy animals (Christiansen et al. 2020; Knowlton et al. 2022; Moore et al. 2021; Pettis et al. 2017).

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whale prey availability and foraging habitat
context_quote: Based on the best available science on ecosystem causation, this Strategy identifies the following conceptual cause-effect impact pathway on female condition and calving rates that could occur if impacts to prey and foraging habitats occur (Figure 2).

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whales from changes to ocean circulation, mixing, and primary/secondary production
context_quote: Recent studies suggest that OSW has the potential to alter local- to regional-scale ocean circulation, including upwelling and downwelling, as well as primary and secondary production (e.g., Daewel et al. 2022; Floeter et al. 2022; National Academies of Sciences 2023; Raghukumar et al. 2023).

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize impacts to North Atlantic right whales from displacement from important habitats, such as calving grounds
geographic_scope: North Atlantic right whale calving grounds and other important habitats
context_quote: Part of this Strategy is to further research the possibility of cause-effect-impact pathways for sublethal effects, such as displacement from calving grounds, impacts of ocean noise, reduced lactation or reduced nursing, and reduced ability to become pregnant or maintain a viable pregnancy.

description: Offshore wind development must implement quieting technology and methods to reduce noise levels during all project phases, with a focus on reducing noise from pile driving and vessel operations
context_quote: With respect to addressing noise impacts, the agencies share a common goal of reducing noise generated during OSW construction and operation (NOAA's Ocean Noise Strategy and BOEM's Center for Marine Acoustics). Though many activities associated with OSW operation and construction produce noise, this Strategy currently focuses on quieting pile-driving and vessel noise.

description: BOEM will develop a quieting performance standard for impact pile driving to set a common goal for providing additional environmental protection, promoting predictability, and driving technological innovation
context_quote: BOEM intends to pursue development of a quieting performance standard for impact pile driving to set a common goal for providing additional environmental protection, promoting predictability, and driving technological innovation.

description: Offshore wind project vessels must implement vessel quieting technologies to reduce noise impacts on North Atlantic right whales
context_quote: Goal 1 includes several actions involving quieting technology and methods (Appendix A) to reduce noise during impact and vibratory pile driving of foundation piles and to encourage integration of vessel quieting technology in new OSW vessels built in the United States.

description: Offshore wind development must avoid or minimize the use of pile driving and unexploded ordnance (UXO) detonations, and if unavoidable, must implement the most effective noise reduction methodologies
context_quote: In order to reduce noise levels during construction, the agencies are committed to working with lessees to develop standards for determining where it would be preferred to use foundation designs that do not rely on pile driving (e.g., gravity-based foundations), as well as to not detonate UXOs when other means of removal are possible.

description: Offshore wind project vessels must maintain a vigilant watch for North Atlantic right whales and slow down, stop, or alter course to avoid striking whales
context_quote: Vessel captains, trained crew members, and PSOs should maintain a vigilant watch for all protected species and slow down, stop their vessel, or alter course, as appropriate and regardless of vessel size, to avoid striking any protected species.

description: Offshore wind project vessels must comply with all North Atlantic right whale vessel speed regulations and approach regulations
context_quote: All OSW-associated vessels must comply with all regulations for the protection of NARWs in effect at the time, including vessel speed regulations and approach regulations (62 FR 6729; 73 FR 60173, 87 FR 46921).

description: Offshore wind development must implement measures to avoid and minimize interactions between North Atlantic right whales and any gear in the water related to construction or operations, including anchor and buoy lines
context_quote: Implement measures designed to avoid and minimize interaction between protected species and any gear in the water that is related to OSW construction or operations, including but not limited to anchor and buoy lines.
